corpus_name: Third Eye AI — Emergency Response Knowledge Base (India)
corpus_description: Curated, paraphrased summaries from official Indian government and WHO publications. Source documents are linked for verification; these summaries are informational and not medical or legal advice.

documents.title: Good Samaritan Rights and Duties of Hospitals/Police
documents.agency: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India

chunks.text: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways describes a Good Samaritan as a bystander who takes a road-accident victim to the nearest hospital or helps by informing the police or medical emergency service.

The Ministry's Good Samaritan information sheet lists rights including protection from civil or criminal liability, permission to leave the hospital immediately, not being forced to furnish personal details, not being compelled to deposit money for the victim's treatment, and receiving an acknowledgement from the hospital.

The Ministry's Good Samaritan information sheet says a Good Samaritan who chooses to be examined by police as a witness should be examined on a single occasion and only after consent. Consult the current official rules for the exact legal procedure; this summary is not legal advice.

documents.title: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 — Section 134A
documents.agency: Government of India, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

chunks.text: Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 defines a Good Samaritan as a person who, in good faith, voluntarily and without expectation of reward or compensation, provides emergency medical or non-medical care or assistance at a motor-vehicle accident scene or transports the victim to a hospital.

Section 134A states that a Good Samaritan is not liable for civil or criminal action for injury to or death of a motor-vehicle accident victim resulting from the Good Samaritan's negligence while rendering emergency medical or non-medical care or assistance, in the circumstances described by the section. The exact legal application should be checked against the current statute and rules; this assistant is not a legal adviser.

documents.title: Emergency Response Services / Patient Transport Service
documents.agency: National Health Mission, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

chunks.text: The National Health Mission describes Dial 108 as predominantly an emergency response ambulance service, primarily designed for critical-care situations, trauma, and road-accident victims.

The National Health Mission describes Dial 102 primarily as basic patient transport, with a focus on pregnant women and children. The NHM source says other categories may also use the service and are not excluded; local service implementation can vary by State or Union Territory.

The National Health Mission notes that 108 and 102 ambulance services operate through State and Union Territory systems. The presence of a national service number does not establish that a vehicle is available, nearby, or dispatched in a particular incident.

documents.title: Global Plan for the Decade of Action for Road Safety 2021–2030
documents.agency: World Health Organization and United Nations Regional Commissions

chunks.text: The WHO and United Nations Regional Commissions developed the Global Plan for the Decade of Action for Road Safety 2021–2030 as a guiding document to support implementation of the Decade's objectives. It is an international policy guidance document, not an operational description of services in a particular Indian district.

The WHO Global Plan promotes a holistic road-safety approach in which safety is central to decisions about road-system design, planning, and management. It provides policy guidance to governments and stakeholders; it does not verify ambulance availability, hospital capacity, or an individual accident.
